Commentary.Commentary: So that's it from us for this game. Australia have finally got back to winning ways and they will hope to continue with the same momentum. With that loss, India have dropped to number two in the ICC ODI rankings but a win in the next game would bring them back on top. Hope you liked our coverage. Join us back for the final ODI on 1st October in Nagpur at 1330 local (0800 GMT). Until then, goodbye and cheers.

Man of the Match, David Warner says that it always feels fantastic to get smile back on the Australian faces. Reckons that he did not get his chance in the past to play ODIs in India but he enjoyed every bit this time as he knows the wickets here quite well. Mentions that they had their mind set on batting deep and they did that really well. Mentions that winning helps in gaining momentum and hopes that this helps them as well.

Steve Smith with a big smile on his face says that it was a nice result. Praises Warner and Finch, who were spectacular and set up the platform for them to get to 330. Mentions that they lost a few wickets again but Handscomb played a handy cameo. Admits that they were too wide with the new ball but pulled things back nicely in the end. On Warner, he says that it's always nice to watch the southpaw, especially in the ODIs, where he has got better with the time and is in spectacular run of form.

Virat Kohli says that the Australians were going strong at the 30-over mark and he was really happy to restrict them around 330. Mentions that his openers did well but none after them could capitalize on the start. Credits Umesh Yadav and Mohammed Shami for bowling really well in the second spell. Informs that spinners might have their off days and this was one of them. Applauds Australia for playing a better brand of cricket today. Adds that bowling slow was the only way to bowl on this wicket. Ends by saying that Australia was the better team on the day.

The Australian bowling lacked discipline at the start but made up for it later on. Kane Richardson led the pace attack, picking up another 3-fer in the series. He was superb with his off-paced deliveries and deceived the batsmen more often than not. Cummins and Coulter-Nile provided a good hand to him with 3 wickets between them and also with some superb death bowling. Head chipped in with some tidy overs too, which kept the scoreboard pressure on the opposition while Zampa got the better of dangerous Pandya once again. Presentation coming up...

Australia came back well after the initial phase but a 78-run stand between Jadhav and Pandya got the chase back on track. The latter departed but it didn't dent the hosts as local lad, Pandey stood tall and rose a 61-run partnership with Jadhav to keep the home side in the hunt. But, both these batsmen fell within 3 deliveries and it paved the way back for the Aussies. They made full use of this as Dhoni couldn't finish things off and the tail couldn't create anything spectacular.

Finally the monkey is off Australia's back as they have ended their winless run away from home. India started the chase superbly. The openers were off to a flier. They added 106 runs with both the batsmen completing their half centuries. Rahane was the first one to fall as he tried to cut loose whereas Sharma fell next due to a confusion in the middle between him and the skipper.
Sigh of relief for the visitors! Good length delivery outside off, Shami swings his bat across but he fails to make contact. AUSTRALIA WIN BY 21 RUNS!
FOUR! Full toss on his hips, Shami smashes that over the mid-wicket region for a boundary. Umesh asks the umpire for a no ball but he is not interested.
Full and angling into the batsman, clipped towards mid-wicket for a single. Smith has a shy at the non-striker's end but he misses. Had he hit, Yadav would have been a goner.

The players are making their way back to the middle. The overs haven't been reduced so nothing has changed. INDIA NEED 77 RUNS OFF 53 BALLS! Adam Zampa to continue bowling to Manish Pandey. Here we go...
The covers have started coming off slowly and it looks as if the resumption is round the corner. It's confirmed - THE MATCH WILL RESUME AT 2100 LOCAL (1530 GMT).

AN UNFORTUNATE STOPPAGE! The players have been asked to leave the field as the rain has picked up. The Indian players are not happy to leave the field and are asking the umpire about it. On the other hand, the Aussies have already left the field. India are 2 runs behind the current DLS par score. The groundstaff have quickly covered the ground.

OUT! Oh dear! A big confusion in the middle results in Rohit Sharma's run out! Pitched outside off, Kohli slashes it towards point. Smith stationed there, leaps to his left, stops the ball and throws it towards striker's end. However, both the batsmen somehow are stranded there. Handscomb doing the back-up, picks up the ball and throws it towards Richardson, who whips the bails off. Sharma is way out of his crease and now has to make the long walk back. The replays show that Kohli had taken a start but seeing Smith stop the ball, he turned back. Rohit, however, sprinted towards the other end. Even if he would have returned from halfway, he would have been safe. India have gifted this wicket to Australia. Massive point in this game. Both the set batsmen are back in the dressing room. Will the Kangaroos make most of this?

Tossed up on middle, spinning away, driven through mid off for a single.
ADAM ZAMPA is brought into the attack now.
Slower through the air around off, spinning away, Rahane drags it through mid-wicket for a single.

Stoinis just stops just before delivering the ball. He is leaving the field and that is surely not a good sign for Australia. The visitors will now have to depend on Finch and Head to finish off his overs. Seems to have hurt his groin during the last ball of his previous over where he tried to stop the ball. AARON FINCH to finish off this over.
Good length delivery around off, punched off the back foot towards mid on.
Angling into the pads, Sharma clips it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller in line of the pads, flicked through square leg for a single.
On a length around off, Rahane clips it towards the fielder at mid-wicket.
Length delivery outside off, carved towards the fielder at point.
Short delivery outside off, Sharma stands tall and defends it towards the fielder at point.
Hurls it fuller outside off, Rohit gets his bat down in time to drive it down the ground.
Back of a length delivery outside off, punched through covers for a single.
Good length delivery around off, dabbed towards third man for a single.
On a fuller length outside off, Rahane prods forward and drives through covers for a single.
Fuller and angling into the pads, eased towards long on for a single.
Powerplay 2 has been signaled by the umpire. Now a maximum of four fielders are allowed outside the circle.
Back of a length delivery outside off, dabbed towards third man for a single.
Angling into the pads, Rahane shuffles across and clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Hurls this fuller outside off, AR prods forward and defends it.
Good length delivery around off, Ajinkya camps back and punches it towards mid on.
Fuller around off, Rahane drives again but this time, straight to the fielder at covers.
FOUR! On a fuller length outside off, Rahane in the mood he is today, will surely not let those go. Camps back a touch and smashes his cut through cover-point for a boundary.
MARCUS STOINIS is introduced into the bowling attack.
Landed on a length outside the line of off stump, Rahane taps it between cover and point to steal a quick single.
FOUR! Now Rahane joins in on the action. Doesn't want to feel left out it seems. Short of a good length around off, Rahane hangs back and pulls this hard over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Stays inside his crease, opens the face and dabs it to point. Straight to the fielder, though.
Tad outside off, run down to third man for a run.

SIX! WHAT A SHOT, ROHIT SHARMA! Wow! Picked the length up early and sent that packing into the stands. Richardson with the short one, Rohit stands tall and muscles the pull over deep mid-wicket for a biggie. Came right off the meat, monstrous hit. With this, the 50-run stand is up as well.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
First bowling change for Australia. KANE RICHARDSON is into the bowling attack.
Ajinkya Rahane comes half-forward and meets the ball with the full face of the bat.
Good length ball very close to off, punched back down towards mid off.
Width on offer outside off, Sharma doesn't want to waste it so he slices that hard. Places it behind point and picks up a run.
On a good length but well outside off, done easily enough by Rahane as he opens the face and dabs it down to third man for a single.
Angling back in on middle and leg, Rahane leans across a touch and flicks it straight to the man at mid-wicket.
Lands it around off, Rahane from deep inside the crease taps it down in front of covers.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Leg bye! Length delivery, angling in, Rahane gets across to flick it away but misses and the ball goes off the pads on the leg side. A leg bye is taken.
Dabbed to point from within the crease.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! Well placed! Full outside off, Rahane opens the face of the bat and glides it past backward point. The third man fielder can't cut it off and the ball races away to the fence.

Length delivery, angling in, Sharma gets across to scoop. Seems to have missed and the ball goes off the hips towards short fine leg. Richardson there makes a good, diving stop. Has a shy at the striker's end and hits but Rahane is safe. Smith enquires about taking a review but the bowler says no. The umpire indicates nothing so there must have been an inside edge involved.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full outside off, pushed to covers.

SIX! Unbelievable! Back of a length, wide outside off, Rahane frees his arms as he slams it hard and flat over covers for a maximum. That was some shot! The Aussie bowling has been poor so far. They are giving too much width.
Ohhh... That was close and needles from Rahane as well! Ajinkya walks across and tries to tuck it past short fine leg. Misses and is lucky that the ball bounces over the sticks.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fullish outswinger outside off, Rahane leans forward and opens the face of the bat, guiding towards backward point, where Smith makes a diving stop.
On a good length outside off, run down to third man for a single.
Length delivery outside off, tapped to covers.
Angling into the batsman, Rahane gets across and looks to play across the line but misses and gets rapped on the thigh pad.
Sensible stuff! Dabs the shortish delivery on the off side behind in front of slip cordon for a quick run.

SIX! Hammered! Back of a length delivery around off, sits nicely for Sharma, who stands and delivers. Pulls it over mid-wicket for a maximum. Rohit loves this shot and has played it to great effect. India are off to a brisk start as well.
Straying on the pads, tucked towards square leg, where Head fields it.
Outside off, Rahane plants his front foot across and leaves it alone.
On a length around off, nips in a touch, Rahane looks to block it but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Length delivery outside off, glided to third man for a single.
Outswinger on a fuller length outside off, left alone.
Sharma covers the stumps, and blocks it on the off side.
FOUR! Slashed! Shortish outside off, Sharma frees his arms and slams it through covers for a boundary. Once again a boundary comes in the over and India tick along nicely.
Angling into the batsman, Sharma dabs it on the leg side and picks up a single.
Pitched fuller outside off, tapped in the cover region.
Length delivery, angling into Sharma, who plants his front foot ahead and tucks it square of the wicket on the leg side for a brace.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Jinx rides the bounce and guides it towards third man for a single.
Rahane pushes with the angle to mid on.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Once again Cummins bowls it full and straight but strays on the pads. Rahane flicks it with utter ease through square leg for a boundary.

Back of a length delivery, angling in. Rahane foes for the pull but the length is not that short to pull. Gets an inside edge onto his thigh. The ball lands beside the track and a quick single is taken.
Slightly fuller around off, Rahane gets across and pushes it to mid on.
Played with an angled bat towards gully.

FOUR! Streaky! Length delivery around off, seams away a touch. Rahane looks to defend with soft hands, gets an outside edge and the ball runs away through the gap between first slip and gully to the fence behind. Even if there was a second slip in place, it wouldn't have carried to him.
Good length delivery around off, nips away a touch, defended from within the crease.
On a good length outside off, glided behind point for a single. Sharma is off the mark on his first delivery.
NATHAN COULTER-NILE to bowl with the second new ball.
Full and angling in, pushed to mid on.

FOUR! Just away from a diving Head! Wide outside off, Rahane slashes it hard. Travis at cover-point, dives to his right but the ball goes past his outstretched hand to the fence behind. Cummins has to keep his line tight!
Angling into the batsman, defended on the leg side.

Full and straight on middle, Rahane flicks it with ease fine down the leg side. Work for Richardson in the deep, who make a sliding stop near the fence, keeping the runs down to a brace. India are off!
A touch fuller this time, around off, defended on the off side.

On a good length outside off, seaming away a touch. Rahane opens the face of the bat and guides it in the backward point region. Both the batsmen take a start but seeing Smith stop the ball with a dive, they decide against the run.

The players have arrived back for the chase. Once again the pair of ROHIT SHARMA and AJINKYA RAHANE will open the innings for India. PAT CUMMINS to start the proceedings with the first new ball. He has a lone slip in place. Here we go...
